minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to pass over the Marshall Park warrant article after the cost estimate rose to about $14 million.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was the Marshall Park project. A new cost estimate far above earlier ones and Select Board opposition led the commission to pass over its town meeting article and to pause construction while design continues. The commission also heard the Recreation director's update and the Polar Plunge plan, approved two invoices, and discussed the revolving fund article and tax-title properties.

presenter, Boys and Girls Club, remote

public_comment.topic: A resident asked for an American flag and the Pledge of Allegiance at meetings, and for a public discussion time on the agenda; he stayed to listen to the Marshall Park discussion.

public_comment.speaker_as_heard: Robert R... Rogers (name partly garbled), 82 Highland Street
public_comment.topic: Doubted the town would support a roughly 15 million dollar project given other town needs. Questioned how much money is on hand, favored doing it right rather than cutting, and discussed phasing and the risk of a stalled second phase.
A resident (a woman, likely Mrs. Rogers) argued residents should get the chance to vote on the project, supported finishing the design, and urged quick decisions on the ARPA money.

votes.outcome: passed (not unanimous; one member said no; count not audible)

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair asked for regular updates on budget accounts, with a walk-through at the first one. The commission settled on quarterly, with a June one before year end.

The recreation director asked whether the commission wants a set contribution to the fair, noting costs like tents, chairs, portable toilets and trash. The chair said she should bring a figure after getting quotes.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park cost estimates and funding plan
budget_items.what_was_said: Estimates rose from the conceptual figure to a later one and then a newest one. The commission planned to request money at town meeting to match the Land and Water Conservation grant.
A per-square-foot estimate for poured rubber surfacing differed greatly between January 2024 and the latest estimate. The speaker said the market rate has been in the low 30s for years.
Phase one was originally thought to be fully funded, but after paid invoices less is available. Value engineering would cut grant-required components and risk the grant contract.

budget_items.topic: Park grant and Land and Water Conservation grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The state said that skipping grant components makes the contract null and void with no reimbursement. The LWCF grant was based on the second estimate, which now looks underestimated.

budget_items.topic: Remaining Marshall Park money including ARPA
budget_items.what_was_said: Remaining funds are a small amount of prior warrant article money plus a million dollars of ARPA. The commission must decide quickly so ARPA money is committed by year end and not lost.
Prior town meeting design appropriations were recited and a remaining balance given.
Commitments for phase one were stated for the OPM firm and the design firm, not all expended. Combined ARPA and design funds remaining were roughly stated.
A member asked what a roughly 15 million dollar project would mean for taxes. The chair said the town accountant could model it by interest rate, term and average tax bill.
A member wants user fees on the November or December agenda because field maintenance costs seem to serve mainly one youth organization.
An invoice for OPM services was approved, in addition to two earlier ones.
An RDLA invoice for September design development labor was approved.

budget_items.topic: Revolving fund article (53D to 53E and a half)
budget_items.what_was_said: The 53D revolving account can hold a limited balance at year end, but the commission has carried more. The article would move the balance to a 53E 1/2 account, and the Attorney General may approve less.

budget_items.topic: Grants and ARPA share of the project
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted grants secured plus ARPA made up a significant share of the project, and the commission would potentially walk away from grant money.

transfers.description: Proposed transfer of the existing balance in the 53D revolving account into a new 53E 1/2 account via the town meeting article; the AG may allow only a limited amount.

decisions.decision: Chris (town finance staff) will be asked to present the first quarterly budget report, with a walk-through, at the next meeting covering the first quarter of FY25.
The recreation director will bring dates and a money figure for the spring vendor fair to the next meeting; May 10 is the preferred date.
The Boys and Girls Club Polar Plunge goes on the next agenda; the Polar Plunge date is November 30, noon to 2, and the club will check with the fire chief on lifeguard needs.
The commission leans toward continuing and completing the design during the pause, to bring an updated cost estimate to the spring town meeting.
User fees will be added to the November agenda; a beach and staffing item is targeted for December.
A special meeting will be held on November 6 to vote on extending consultant design work; the chair will gather fee information beforehand.
The chair will notify sports users, the schools superintendent and the sports director, and the park grant and LWCF grant contacts.
The commission has no interest in any of the tax-taking list properties; the chair will email back no interest. No vote was taken.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to pass over its Marshall Park article at the special town meeting after a new cost estimate came in far above earlier ones.
The commission leans toward finishing the design during the pause, to bring an updated cost estimate to the spring town meeting.
The commission voted, not unanimously, to tell youth baseball, softball and Little League users the fields will be available this spring because construction will not proceed.
A special meeting is set for November 6 to vote on extending consultant design work, and the chair will notify the grant contacts.
The commission approved the Scansa invoice for owner's project manager services and the RDLA invoice for September design development work.

why_it_matters: The Marshall Park project will not be on the special town meeting warrant, so residents will not vote on it this fall; the question is expected to return at the spring town meeting.
The state said skipping grant-required parts voids the park grant contract with no reimbursement, and the ARPA money has a year-end commitment deadline, so the decision is time-limited.
Any local share of the project would be raised through taxes; a member asked about the tax effect and the chair said the town accountant could model it, but no figure has been produced.
watch_next: November 6 special meeting: a vote on extending consultant design work, with fee information from the chair beforehand.
The next meeting: the first quarterly budget report with a walk-through, and the Boys and Girls Club Polar Plunge on the agenda (event set for November 30).
